Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage is dominated by the dramatic AI stock selloff that intensified after Anthropic's volatile IPO debut, wiping out trillions in market value and prompting emergency stabilization measures across Asian markets. Secondary threads include fallout from the Jensen Huang/Nvidia chip-smuggling scandal, a major bank accounting lapse at Citi, and scattered policy and corporate stories.

stories.headline: AI Stock Selloff Deepens After Anthropic's Turbulent IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic's shares, which popped 17% on their Nasdaq debut, cratered to within a nickel of their IPO price days later as the broader market suffered a roughly $4 trillion AI-driven wipeout, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq falling into correction territory and the VIX topping 30 for the first time since March.

stories.headline: Asia's Stock Rescue Efforts Gather Pace After Wall Street Plunge
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports Asian authorities are stepping up efforts to stem a deepening stock-market rout, with China easing margin requirements and Taiwan and South Korea rolling out intervention measures following Friday's global plunge in equities.

stories.headline: Citi Undercounted $35 Billion in Assets at U.K. Subsidiary
stories.summary: WSJ reports that Citi's record-keeping blunder, tied to risk-weighted assets, is a setback for CEO Jane Fraser's push to strengthen the bank's internal controls.

stories.headline: The Alice Huang Associate Accused of Funneling Nvidia Chips to China
stories.summary: WSJ and FT detail how a defendant in a chip-smuggling case worked with Jensen Huang's romantic partner, Alice Huang, amid wider fallout from the scandal that has rattled Nvidia and the broader AI trade.

stories.headline: Judge Approves $7.25 Billion Roundup Cancer Settlement
stories.summary: A judge approved Bayer's $7.25 billion settlement over its Roundup weed killer, which the company called a "decisive milestone," though the debate over whether the product causes cancer is unlikely to end.

stories.headline: Procter & Gamble to Increase Factory Shifts Without Humans to Cut Costs
stories.summary: NYT reports the maker of Pampers and Bounty paper towels already operates 15 sites capable of running shifts unattended, with plans to add more such automated shifts in 2027.

stories.headline: UBS Capital Fight Enters Final Round as Lawmakers Resume Debate
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports the fight over UBS Group's future capital requirements is heading for a showdown in the Swiss parliament, with odds tilted toward defeat for the global wealth manager.

Business.gaps: Puck had no business/markets coverage visible in searches or feeds; Politico and The Economist feed items skewed toward politics/geopolitics rather than markets news in this window.

US politics.overview: Coverage is dominated by the lame-duck congressional sprint: Hakeem Jeffries' path to becoming the first Black House speaker, an intensifying standoff over Iran-war funding that could trigger a December 11 government shutdown, and the Senate Democratic leadership fight between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen. Trump's return from his Asia trip and a sprawling White House press conference touching on 2028 politics also drew heavy attention.

stories.headline: House Democrats formally nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker
stories.summary: House Democrats voted 251-11 in a closed-door caucus ballot to nominate Jeffries for speaker, putting him comfortably above the 218 votes needed on the House floor Jan. 3, though progressive critics flooded members with calls urging them to oppose him.

stories.headline: Why a shutdown is getting more likely
stories.summary: With funding running out Dec. 11, Punchbowl reports House and Senate Democrats are split on whether to use the deadline to choke off Iran-war funding, and Republicans and Democratic leaders remain far apart on a bipartisan agreement.

stories.headline: The latest from Trump's press conference
stories.summary: Trump gave a wide-ranging White House press conference after returning from Asia, where he met Xi and Putin, and the briefing doubled as an early audition for JD Vance and Marco Rubio's 2028 ambitions, according to a Wall Street Journal account aggregated by RealClearPolitics.

stories.headline: Van Hollen says it's still a 'wide-open race' for majority leader
stories.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen said the contest to lead Senate Democrats remains unsettled as he continues challenging Chuck Schumer for the post, a fight Punchbowl News says is unfolding as Democrats try to organize an expected 56-seat majority.

stories.headline: Pandemic-era law passed unconstitutionally because of proxy voting, appeals court rules
stories.summary: The 5th Circuit upheld a Texas injunction against pregnant-worker accommodations by ruling that a massive Biden-era funding bill was unconstitutionally passed using proxy voting, a decision with broad implications for other pandemic-era legislation.

stories.headline: Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
stories.summary: Trump directed federal contractors to consult the White House before responding to congressional inquiries and to withhold communications the administration deems privileged, raising new oversight friction ahead of a Democratic-controlled House.

stories.headline: Trump signs bill to halt penny production
stories.summary: Trump signed legislation formally ending penny production, requiring cash transactions to round to the nearest nickel, a symbolic but tangible policy change covered as the penny's official demise.

stories.headline: Washington governor decries 'out-of-control' ICE at Seattle airport
stories.summary: Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson condemned ICE operations at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport after masked federal agents detained two people over the weekend, amid broader friction between Democratic state officials and federal immigration enforcement.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS and Cook Political Report had no items from the last 24-48 hours in search results (most recent NOTUS content found was weeks old); Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian coverage was limited to the specific feed items provided since these outlets block web search.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and AI outlets remains dominated by the fallout from Anthropic's turbulent IPO debut and the broader AI-stock selloff, compounded by lingering questions about ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's potential return. Several outlets are also digging into AI safety and supply-chain security research (METR capability benchmarks, leaky AI routers), a contested Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis, and fresh hacks hitting US federal agencies.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO Triumph Turns Turbulent
stories.summary: The Information reported Anthropic's stock jumped as much as 39% above its IPO price before settling to close up 17% at $97.17 on its debut, giving it a $1.76 trillion market cap, but shares slid on the second day after banks exercised the 'greenshoe' option.

stories.headline: AI Selloff Wipes Out Trillions, Erases Nasdaq's 2026 Gains
stories.summary: The Guardian reported the Nasdaq lost trillions in value as investors questioned the scale of AI infrastructure spending, with Anthropic's record IPO unable to stem the rout; WSJ separately described the selloff as reminiscent of the dot-com bust and noted a '$4 trillion AI wipeout,' while Bloomberg reported China's AI stock trade has also turned into a '$1.7 trillion' rout.

stories.headline: Can Jensen Huang Really Come Back to Nvidia?
stories.summary: The Information examined whether Jensen Huang, who resigned amid an affair scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy, could return to Nvidia, while TechCrunch described a split picture between strong earnings and executives publicly pushing for his comeback, and FT drew a historical parallel warning about concentrated power at the top.

stories.headline: METR Report Shows AI Capability Growth Is Outpacing Ability to Test Safety
stories.summary: MIT Technology Review covered a new METR report finding some AI capabilities keep improving exponentially even as models become harder to reliably evaluate; The Decoder's version of the same research warned that leading models like Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra are improving rapidly at research tasks while current data can't rule out a dangerous capability jump, and The Information noted METR found AIs can now outperform humans at week-length tasks.

stories.headline: AI Inference Supply Chain Found Leaking User Data and Stealing Keys
stories.summary: Ars Technica reported that security researchers used two million fake AI requests with trackable canary credentials to show that supposedly private data doesn't stay private across cheap AI inference providers; The Decoder's version said researchers at Dragos found at least three compromised providers along with hundreds of stolen AWS keys.

stories.headline: FBI and USDA Databases Reportedly Hacked
stories.summary: The Verge reported both the FBI and the US Department of Agriculture were hacked, noting this is the second such incident reported recently; TechCrunch added that President Trump called the reported FBI National Crime Information Center breach 'not good.'

stories.headline: Claude-Assisted Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis Sparks Dispute
stories.summary: The Decoder reported that Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge said he used Claude to help prove the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis, with the Lean and Mathlib communities later confirming the proof correct after independent verification of 17 million lines of code; The Information and The Economist also covered the milestone, while a competing all-human Stanford draft emerged hours later.

stories.headline: AI Server Makers Hike Prices Up to 45% Mid-Contract
stories.summary: FT reported that AI server suppliers including Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro are demanding substantially higher prices from buyers months after contracts were signed, with increased costs hitting trading firms; Techmeme flagged the same FT report as a top story.

Tech & AI.gaps: Could not retrieve recent material from Google DeepMind's own announcements page, or directly from OpenAI's and Anthropic's own blogs (only third-party coverage of them was found); The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist and The Guardian were reported only from the provided feed items since they block web search.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are dominated by the fate of the bipartisan US permitting reform bill (BAAJA) now headed to a divided House after Senate passage, alongside the contentious, deadlock-prone COP31 climate summit in Antalya. Several outlets are also tracking winter grid reliability, falling US power-sector emissions despite coal subsidies, and corporate climate retrenchment (Meta) amid the AI-driven data center boom.

stories.headline: Permitting reform bill heads to House as Democratic divisions persist
stories.summary: The Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act to overhaul federal energy permitting, but Utility Dive reports some Democrats object to its changes to environmental law and tribal authority while others see it as the best available deal. Bloomberg similarly reported the Senate approved the measure 62-33, sending it to a House where its fate is uncertain, while Heatmap, Canary Media and Latitude Media all detailed the bill's rocky path, including opposition from tribal organizations like NATHPO and the National Congress of American Indians.

stories.headline: COP31 draft deal drops fossil-fuel language as talks near deadline
stories.summary: Carbon Brief reports the COP31 summit in Antalya is deeply divided, with a revised draft text dropping references to ending fossil fuel use and weakening adaptation finance language just before the conference's scheduled close. A third draft was expected as ministers held late-night 'divan' discussions seeking common ground on issues from the next IPCC report timing to climate finance.

stories.headline: Tribal sovereignty emerges as a key sticking point in the permitting debate
stories.summary: Canary Media reports that while climate advocates debated the permitting bill's emissions impact, tribal sovereignty proved the bigger sticking point in the Senate, with groups like NATHPO urging the House to reject the bill and start over with direct tribal consultation. Not all tribal organizations are opposed, however, as the National Tribal Energy Association backs provisions it says would unlock tribal energy potential.

stories.headline: The U.A.E. Is Shuttling Oil Past Iran in Risky Hormuz Operation
stories.summary: WSJ reports on a high-stakes UAE shuttle operation, backed by U.S. military assistance, aimed at moving oil past Iran's grip on the Hormuz waterway.

stories.headline: US power sector emissions set to fall despite record demand and pro-coal push
stories.summary: Canary Media reports that despite record electricity demand and Trump administration efforts to prop up coal plants, US power sector CO2 emissions are on track to decline this year, driven by a 10% drop in coal burn through July per Energy Innovation analysis. That marks a reversal from 2025, when coal generation jumped 13% amid a surge in demand and high gas prices.

stories.headline: Winter grid outlook improves, but elevated blackout risk lingers in a few regions
stories.summary: Latitude Media reports NERC found only three North American regions at elevated blackout risk this winter, down from seven a year ago, though the Carolinas remain at risk amid growing electric heating and data center loads. Utility Dive separately reported FERC's winter outlook found improved market coordination in the West could offset low hydropower from drought, while New England risks over-reliance on oil.

stories.headline: Meta reconsiders its 2030 net-zero goal amid AI emissions surge
stories.summary: Heatmap reports that Meta's newly released 2026 sustainability report says the company is "re-evaluating" its net-zero by 2030 goal amid a 45% year-over-year rise in its emissions, deepening skepticism about its climate commitments relative to peers like Google and Microsoft.

stories.headline: Trump administration issues 7th emergency order keeping Michigan coal plant alive
stories.summary: Heatmap reports the Department of Energy issued a seventh emergency order under the Federal Power Act mandating that the coal-fired J.H. Campbell plant in Michigan, owned by Consumers Energy, stay open to prevent blackouts on the MISO grid despite its planned retirement.

Energy.gaps: Argus Media's available coverage was outdated (no stories found within the last 48 hours). Reuters, NYT, and The Economist block web search and no recent feed items were provided for them beyond secondhand mentions inside Carbon Brief's roundups, so direct independent coverage from those three outlets could not be confirmed.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: The dominant story across nearly every outlet is the deep AI-driven selloff rocking Asian equities, with Beijing, Taipei and Seoul rushing out stabilization measures, compounded by fallout from Nvidia's leadership crisis and accounting scrutiny. Geopolitics coverage centers on the aftermath of the Xi-Trump-Putin Shenzhen summit and shifting US-China power dynamics, while Chinese tech outlets highlight a wave of domestic AI model and chip announcements amid the market turmoil.

stories.headline: China, Taiwan and South Korea scramble to stem AI-driven stock rout
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports Asian authorities are stepping up intervention after Wall Street's AI-stock plunge, with China easing margin requirements and Taiwan and South Korea rolling out their own rescue measures; SCMP notes that on the mainland the CSI 300 sank 0.8% and the chip-heavy Star 50 index slumped 3.1% as the selloff complicated Beijing's efforts to put a floor under stocks.

stories.headline: Nvidia turmoil deepens with US accounting probe and Jensen Huang affair fallout
stories.summary: US securities regulators are reportedly investigating Nvidia's accounting practices, adding to turmoil at the chipmaker following CEO Jensen Huang's resignation; Caixin's continuing investigation has focused on the former Megaspeed executive linked to Huang, noting she faced scrutiny over a reported relationship with Huang and allegations she disclosed U.S. information.

stories.headline: China's $1.7 trillion AI stock trade turns into a losing bet
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that China's once red-hot AI stock trade has reversed sharply; Nikkei Asia similarly notes that mounting concerns over the profitability of artificial intelligence are weighing on Chinese stock markets despite home-grown AI being crucial to the country's strategy of technological self-reliance.

stories.headline: Trump defends Shenzhen summit with Xi and Putin amid backlash
stories.summary: Trump defended his summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin as he returned from China to face criticism at home, while SCMP's commentary argues that the historic Shenzhen meeting and its four-point statement was never meant to produce a 'grand bargain.'

stories.headline: Top CNPC shale gas executive placed under corruption investigation
stories.summary: Xie Jun, a deputy general manager of state energy giant China National Petroleum Corp, is under investigation for suspected corruption, China's top anti-graft watchdog announced.

stories.headline: Taiwan's parties make final push before Nov. 28 local elections
stories.summary: Candidates across Taiwan stepped up campaigning a week before local elections, with Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an sharing a stage with Ko Wen-je while DPP mayoral candidates for Taipei and New Taipei planned a joint rally; the KMT and TPP have also agreed not to field competing candidates in some races to improve their chances against the DPP.

stories.headline: US power edge over China in Asia narrows to record low
stories.summary: China has narrowed its power gap with the US in Asia to a record low in an Australian think tank's annual index, which attributes much of the shift to Washington's own diplomatic 'missteps'; Bloomberg separately reports the US advantage has shrunk further amid fallout from the Iran war and unilateralism.

stories.headline: Chinese tech giants push out new AI models and chips amid market jitters
stories.summary: Tencent released the open weights of its flagship Hy4 AI model, allowing developers to download and deploy it themselves, while Alibaba said it is using chips from its own semiconductor subsidiary T-Head to train its next Qwen model.

China.gaps: Could not find distinct, recent-24-48h coverage from Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Rest of World, China Daily, Xinhua, CGTN, Yicai Global or ChinaTalk beyond what's in the feed; search access to Global Times and Caixin surfaced mostly older or evergreen content rather than fresh 24-48h leads.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Regional coverage is dominated by the escalating Iran-Gulf conflict, with Iran striking a civilian facility in Bahrain and hitting tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, prompting a wave of condemnations from Gulf states. Secondary attention is on the collapse of COP31 climate talks in Turkey and a surge in settler violence in the occupied West Bank, while business desks are tracking Gulf sovereign wealth and property deals amid the war's economic fallout.

stories.headline: Iran strikes Bahrain industrial site, tankers hit in Hormuz as Gulf tensions spike
stories.summary: Bahrain said two people were injured, one critically, after an Iranian strike hit a civilian industrial facility on Sitra Island, while two tankers were separately struck in the Strait of Hormuz and the IRGC claimed to have downed another US drone. Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar and Jordan all condemned the attack as a violation of Bahrain's sovereignty.

stories.headline: COP31 talks collapse in Turkey as EU rejects final draft deal
stories.summary: The UN climate summit in Antalya became the longest-ever COP after negotiations broke down on Sunday, with the European Union and other countries rejecting a compromise text over fossil fuel language.

stories.headline: Israeli settlers attack Palestinian villages as Eisenkot blames Ben Gvir and Smotrich
stories.summary: Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot condemned a wave of settler arson attacks in the occupied West Bank as "Jewish terrorism in every sense," blaming ministers Smotrich and Ben Gvir, after Al Jazeera reported attacks on villages in Ramallah and el-Bireh that included the burning of a dozen vehicles.

stories.headline: UAE runs risky shuttle service to move oil past Iran in Hormuz
stories.summary: The WSJ reports the UAE is running a high-stakes oil shuttle operation with US military assistance to break Iran's grip on the Strait of Hormuz, underscoring how central the waterway has become to the broader war's economic stakes.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia's $1trn PIF wealth fund faces identity crisis amid war pressures
stories.summary: The Economist examines how Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund is being pulled in multiple directions, strained not only by the regional war but by broader questions over its strategic focus and spending priorities.

stories.headline: Dubai's Nakheel raises Dh5.5bn after selling out first phase of Palm Springs project
stories.summary: Dubai developer Nakheel raised Dh5.5 billion after fully selling out the first phase of its new Palm Springs residential project, a sign of continued strength in the emirate's property market.

stories.headline: Syria destroys 400 million captagon pills in major drug haul
stories.summary: Syrian authorities destroyed some 400 million captagon pills in a large-scale crackdown, part of an ongoing effort to dismantle the narcotics trade linked to the former regime.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not independently verify recent coverage from AGBI (search returned mostly month-old items), Arabian Business beyond PIF/Houthi items already dated Nov 18-19, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, The New Arab, Times of Israel, Ynetnews, Haaretz, or Iran International beyond the Hormuz shipping-data story already cited; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT and BBC are search-blocked so only feed items (none provided for most) were used.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage over the past 48 hours centers on the escalating Ethiopia-Eritrea border crisis and Wagner's entanglement in Central African Republic peace talks, alongside major economic developments including Senegal's IMF bailout troubles, a Southern Africa mining royalty push, and fallout from South Africa's local elections. African Business, TechCabal and Mining Weekly also highlight fintech growth and mineral-sector deals reshaping investment flows across the continent.

stories.headline: Ethiopia-Eritrea: Why Badme, the town that sparked a bloody war, is back in the firing line
stories.summary: Eritrean troops have retaken the border town of Badme amid drone strikes and heavy shelling, reviving fears of a full-scale war 25 years after the town was awarded to Asmara, as Ethiopia's push for Red Sea access deepens the rift. Al Jazeera has separately tracked weeks of accusations between Addis Ababa and Asmara, including severed diplomatic ties and warnings from analysts that the conflict risks becoming a regional war.

stories.headline: Central African Republic: How Wagner's gold stands in the way of peace
stories.summary: Talks between Bangui and N'Djamena over the return of three rebel CAR leaders sheltering in Chad are dragging on, with Wagner's gold interests in the country complicating a resolution.

stories.headline: Zille blocked from Johannesburg mayoralty by ActionSA-ANC deal
stories.summary: A deal between the ANC and ActionSA appears set to exclude the DA's Helen Zille from Johannesburg's mayoralty even though her party won the most votes in the city, part of a broader municipal power-sharing scramble that Africa Confidential reports has also seen the ANC offer mayoralties to keep the DA out of other metros.

stories.headline: Senegal's budget defeat puts $2.2bn IMF rescue in jeopardy
stories.summary: A political feud between Senegal's president and a former premier has stalled a debt overhaul, with bond investors punishing Dakar as the country's $2.2 billion IMF rescue hangs in the balance; Africanews separately reports the president is bypassing parliament to push the bailout forward.

stories.headline: Côte d'Ivoire to raise mineral-royalty rates before IMF talks
stories.summary: Citing Bloomberg, Mining Weekly reports Côte d'Ivoire plans to raise royalties paid by mining companies to boost government revenue ahead of potential talks with the IMF on new financing.

stories.headline: Angola seeks 10% stake in De Beers under Anglo's proposed exit
stories.summary: Citing Reuters, Mining Weekly reports Angola is seeking a 10% holding in De Beers, reportedly valued around $180 million, as part of Anglo American's planned sale of its stake in the diamond producer.

stories.headline: African instant payments hit $1.8 trillion a year as transactions triple
stories.summary: A new AfricaNenda/UN Economic Commission for Africa report finds instant payment systems processed 71.4 billion transactions worth $1.8 trillion in 2025, almost triple 2021 volumes, even as trust issues keep many users reliant on cash.

stories.headline: Moniepoint MFB opens Northern regional headquarters in physical banking push
stories.summary: Moniepoint has commissioned a new North Central regional headquarters in Abuja as Nigeria's central bank pushes nationally licensed microfinance banks to expand their physical branch presence.

Africa.gaps: The Continent had no distinct recent stories surfaced in search; Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block web search and none of their Africa-specific items appeared in the provided feed, so they could not be independently verified beyond items referenced secondhand by other outlets.

Media.overview: Media coverage over the past 48 hours centers on upheaval inside Skydance-owned news divisions (CBS News buyouts, an unreported Musk investment) alongside a fresh wave of journalism layoffs in the UK and US, plus notable TV-news talent moves and AI-related media policy debates.

stories.headline: Skydance confirms Elon Musk is a shareholder, but CNN and CBS News stay silent
stories.summary: David Ellison acknowledged on stage with Andrew Ross Sorkin that Elon Musk is now a Skydance investor, a disclosure that Status reports Skydance-owned CNN and CBS News have not mentioned to their own viewers.

stories.headline: Dozens of CBS News staffers take buyouts in 'extinction level' exodus
stories.summary: Status reports that a wave of buyout acceptances has hollowed out CBS News' foreign desk and rippled across '60 Minutes,' the Washington bureau and the Evening News under Bari Weiss and Skydance.

stories.headline: Journalism job cuts tracker: People Inc. cuts 195 jobs, Telegraph to cut around 100
stories.summary: Press Gazette's ongoing tracker of 2026 newsroom layoffs logs major new cuts, including roughly 195 jobs at People Inc. and about 100 at the Telegraph.

stories.headline: Robert Winnett leaves Telegraph after 19 years to join Daily Mail
stories.summary: Press Gazette reports that Robert Winnett, who had been deputy editor at The Telegraph for over a decade, is departing for the Daily Mail.

stories.headline: Willie Geist to leave MS NOW, commit full-time to NBC News
stories.summary: Adweek notes Geist's exit as Skydance CEO David Ellison reiterates that CBS News and CNN will keep operating as separate units; Status separately reported the move capped months of negotiation tied to the NBCU-Versant split.

stories.headline: Milwaukee Journal Sentinel sued over thinly sourced story, reporter accused of relationship with subject
stories.summary: CJR examines a lawsuit against the Journal Sentinel after it published allegations against a candidate who responded by claiming he'd had a relationship with one of the paper's reporters; the paper says it stands by reporting that went through standard editing and legal review.

stories.headline: Kaitlan Collins' absence from Bill Maher's 'Real Time' finale tied to White House press conference
stories.summary: Deadline reports the CNN anchor was held up covering a White House press conference, forcing a last-minute guest swap on Maher's season finale.

stories.headline: CAA's Bryan Lourd pushes Congress to pass NO FAKES Act amid AI cloning fears
stories.summary: The CAA chief argued performers and creators need legal protections over their likeness as AI cloning tools proliferate across the entertainment industry.

Media.gaps: Puck, Poynter, NYT, WSJ, FT and The Guardian yielded no fresh 24-48h media-industry items beyond what's listed (Guardian's feed item was unrelated to media); Poynter could not be found via search.
